'''Emmanuel Carvallo''' (1856–1945) was a French [[mathematician]] born in [[Narbonne]].<ref>{{cite book
| title = Changing images in mathematics: from the French Revolution to the new millennium 
| first1 = Umberto |last1 = Bottazzini |author-link=Umberto Bottazzini | first2 = Amy | last2 = Dahan-Dalmédico
| year = 2001
| pages = 162
| publisher = Routledge}}</ref> He is notable for showing in 1897 that [[bicycle]]s could be [[Bicycle and motorcycle dynamics#Self-stability|self-stable]],<ref name="KMPRS">{{cite journal 
| journal = [[Science (journal)|Science]]  
| first1 = J. D. G. | last1 = Kooijman | first2 = J. P. | last2= Meijaard|first3= J. M. |last3=Papadopoulos|first4= A.|last4= Ruina|first5= A. L.|last5= Schwab 
| title = A bicycle can be self-stable without gyroscopic or caster effects 
| url = http://bicycle.tudelft.nl/stablebicycle/StableBicyclev34Revised.pdf 
| volume = 332 
| issue = 6027 
| pages = 339–342 
| doi = 10.1126/science.1201959 
| format = PDF 
| date = April 15, 2011
| accessdate = 2011-04-16 | bibcode=2011Sci...332..339K | pmid = 21493856
}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
| url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/science-news/3296637/The-mathematical-way-to-ride-a-bike.html
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101124045643/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/science/science-news/3296637/The-mathematical-way-to-ride-a-bike.html
| url-status = dead
| archive-date = 2010-11-24
| title = The mathematical way to ride a bike
| first = Roger | last= Highfield
| date = Jun 2007 
| journal = [[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]]
| accessdate = 2011-04-16}}</ref><ref name="MPRS">{{cite journal
 |journal         = [[Proceedings of the Royal Society A]]
 |volume          = 463
 |issue           = 2084
 |year            = 2007
 |pages           = 1955–1982
 |url             = https://audiophile.tam.cornell.edu/~als93/Publications/06PA0459BicyclePaperv45.pdf
 |title           = Linearized dynamics equations for the balance and steer of a bicycle: a benchmark and review
 |author          = J. P. Meijaard
 |author2         = J. M. Papadopoulos
 |author3         = A. Ruina
 |author4         = A. L. Schwab
 |name-list-style = amp
 |doi             = 10.1098/rspa.2007.1857
 |format          = PDF
 |bibcode         = 2007RSPSA.463.1955M
 |url-status         = dead
 |archiveurl      = https://web.archive.org/web/20110501062456/http://audiophile.tam.cornell.edu/~als93/Publications/06PA0459BicyclePaperv45.pdf
 |archivedate     = 2011-05-01
}}</ref> for opposing [[Electromagnetic radiation#Wave model|wave models]] of [[X-ray]]s in 1900,<ref>{{citation|page=42|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ULH7S4j8rlMC&pg=PA42|title=The Tiger and the Shark: Empirical Roots of Wave-Particle Dualism|first=Bruce R.|last=Wheaton|publisher=Cambridge University Press|year=1991|isbn=978-0-521-35892-7}}.</ref> and for claiming in 1912 that [[Albert Einstein|Einstein's]] [[Theory of Relativity]] had been proven false.<ref>{{cite journal
| magazine = Theosophical Path Magazine
| title = Science and Research
| date = January 1935
| author = C. J. Ryan
| page = 518}}</ref>
